sn47.8:1.1: i. The incompetent cook “Bhikkhus, suppose a foolish, incompetent, unskilful cook were to present a king or a royal minister with various kinds of curries:
sn47.8:1.2: sour, bitter, pungent, sweet, sharp, mild, salty, bland.
sn47.8:2.1: “That foolish, incompetent, unskilful cook does not pick up the sign of his own master’s preference:
sn47.8:2.2: ‘Today this curry pleased my master, or he reached for this one, or he took a lot of this one, or he spoke in praise of this one;
sn47.8:2.3: or the sour curry pleased my master today, or he reached for the sour one, or he took a lot of the sour one, or he spoke in praise of the sour one; or the bitter curry … or the pungent curry … or the sweet curry … or the sharp curry … or the mild curry … or the salty curry … or the bland curry pleased my master … or he spoke in praise of the bland one.’
sn47.8:3.1: “That foolish, incompetent, unskilful cook does not gain gifts of clothing, wages, and bonuses.
sn47.8:3.3: Because that foolish, incompetent, unskilful cook does not pick up the sign of his own master’s preference.
sn47.8:3.4: “So too, bhikkhus, here some foolish, incompetent, unskilful bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.8:3.5: While he dwells contemplating the body in the body, his mind does not become concentrated, his corruptions are not abandoned,
sn47.8:3.6: he does not pick up that sign.
sn47.8:3.7: He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings …
sn47.8:3.9: phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.8:3.10: While he dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, his mind does not become concentrated, his corruptions are not abandoned,
sn47.8:3.11: he does not pick up that sign.
sn47.8:4.1: “That foolish, incompetent, unskilful bhikkhu does not gain pleasant dwellings in this very life, nor does he gain mindfulness and clear comprehension.
sn47.8:4.3: Because, bhikkhus, that foolish, incompetent, unskilful bhikkhu does not pick up the sign of his own mind.
sn47.8:5.1: ii. The competent cook “Suppose, bhikkhus, a wise, competent, skilful cook were to present a king or a royal minister with various kinds of curries:
sn47.8:5.2: sour, bitter, pungent, sweet, sharp, mild, salty, bland.
sn47.8:6.1: “That wise, competent, skilful cook picks up the sign of his own master’s preference:
sn47.8:6.2: ‘Today this curry pleased my master … or he spoke in praise of the bland one.’
sn47.8:7.1: “That wise, competent, skilful cook gains gifts of clothing, wages, and bonuses.
sn47.8:7.3: Because that wise, competent, skilful cook picks up the sign of his own master’s preference.
sn47.8:7.4: “So too, bhikkhus, here some wise, competent, skilful bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.8:7.5: While he dwells contemplating the body in the body, his mind becomes concentrated, his corruptions are abandoned,
sn47.8:7.7: He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings …
sn47.8:7.9: phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.8:7.10: While he dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, his mind becomes concentrated, his corruptions are abandoned,
sn47.8:8.1: “That wise, competent, skilful bhikkhu gains pleasant dwellings in this very life, and he gains mindfulness and clear comprehension.
sn47.8:8.3: Because, bhikkhus, that wise, competent, skilful bhikkhu picks up the sign of his own mind.”
